FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Utensils, 
Cutlery and Domestic Hardware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division 
Council. 


In this amalgamated standard, the material has been modified keeping in view the availability of the indigenous 
materials and certain other changes which would help in implementing the Indian Standard in a better way. 


This standard has been formulated by amalgamating IS 992 : 1964 ‘Specification for forks (table, fish, pastry and 
serving) stainless steel’ and IS 993 : 1964 ‘Specification for forks (table, fish, pastry and serving) brass and 
nickel silver’. All these standards would be withdrawn after publication of this standard. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16218 : 2014 


Indian Standard 
FORKS — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers the requirements for the following 
types of forks made from stainless steel and nickel 
silver plated with brass as a parent material with or 
without plastic handle: 


a) Table/Serving fork, 
b) Dessert fork, 

c) Fish fork, and 

d) Pastry fork. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below. 


IS No. Title 

422 : 2006 Specification for brass sheet and strip 
for the manufacture of utensils 
(second revision)

decorative and protective purposes

(first revision) 

15997 : 2012 Low nickel austenitic stainless steel 
sheet and strip for utensils and 
kitchen appliances — Specification 

3 MATERIAL 


Material for forks shall be as under. 


3.1 SS 304 (see IS 6911), grades of IS 15997 or any 
food grade stainless steel. 


3.2 Brass as parent material (see IS 422) and plated 
with pure silver as per IS 1959. 


3.3 Plastic handle shall be free from deleterious 
substances, resist the action of diluted organic acids 


and should not be inflammable as to burst into flames 
when a lightened match is applied to it. 


4 SHAPES AND DIMENSIONS 


4.1 The forks shall be manufactured in one piece either 
with solid handle forged or cast with prongs or pressed 
into shape. The forks may be manufactured also with 
hollow handle or with plastics handle. The design of 
the handles of forks shall be as agreed to between the 
manufacturer and the purchaser. When spoons, forks 
and knives are required to be supplied in sets, the design 
on the handles and general appearance of the item in a 
set shall match. 


4.2 The fork shall conform to shapes and dimensions 
given in 4.3 to 4.8, however the detailed specifications 
are left to the discretion of manufacturers and are 
subject to the agreement with the purchaser. 


4.3 Table/Serving and Dessert Fork, Solid Handle 
(see Fig. 1 A) 


4.4 Table/Serving and Dessert Fork, Pressed 
Handle (see Fig. 1 B) 


4.5 Fish Fork, Solid Handle (see Fig. 2 A) 

4.6 Fish Fork, Pressed Handle (see Fig. 2 B) 
4.7 Pastry Fork, Solid Handle (see Fig. 3 A) 
4.8 Pastry Fork, Pressed Handle (see Fig. 3 B)

5 MANUFACTURE 


5.1 The forks with solid or pressed handles shall be 
made in one piece.

Fic. 3 Pastry Fork 


5.2 The forks with hollow handles shall have the 
prongs forged the tangs well drawn. The scales shall 
fit closely to the tang and shall be finished flush and 
smooth. The joints shall be properly silver-soldered in 
case of nickel silver hollow handles and welded in case 
of stainless steel hollow handles. 


5.3 Where the plastics handles, are cast, they shall be 
soundly moulded with the tang in position. The tang 
shall be properly shaped and groove. The end of the 
tangs shall be properly shaped and grooved. The end 
of the tangs shall be at least 15 mm away from the free 


end. When plastics handles are fitted, the length of the 
tang shall be at least 65 mm to ensure rigid fixing. 


6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


6.1 Workmanship 


The forks shall be free from burrs, seams, cracks or 
other manufacturing defects. All edges shall be well 
rounded or chamfered. The prongs shall be evenly 
tapered to the point. The prongs shall be suitably and 
evenly flattened or pointed at the tip of the prongs. 


The handle of the fork and the cup of the fork 
containing the prongs shall be in good alignment. 


6.2 Finish 
6.2.1 The finishing of the fork shall be mirror all over. 


6.2.2 The nickel silver forks are made as per 3.2. 
Nickel is plated on the brass up to 15 microns thickness 
which acts as bonding with parent metal brass and the 
silver. Silver is plated on the nickel base which gives 
better bonding effect. Plating thickness of the silver 
shall be minimum 40 micron. Purity of silver shall not 
be less than 99.0 percent. Effective anti-tarnishing 
process shall be used after silver plating to avoid 
oxidation of silver used for better life or the plating 
shall conform to IS 1067. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Staining Test 


The surface of fork shall be thoroughly washed with 
hot soapy water. Thoroughly rinse and then degrease 
the test specimen in acetone or methyleted spirit, then 
wiped with soft cloth. The fork, when dipped for 16 h 
in each of the following solutions, shall not show any 
sign of staining after removal from each solution at 
the end of above period: 


a) Ten grams of glacial acetic acid (99 percent) 
conforming to IS 695 dissolved in distilled water 
conforming to IS 1070 to make 100 ml, and 

b) Five grams of pure sodium chloride 
conforming to IS 4408 dissolved in distilled 
water to make 100 ml. 


7.2 Bending Test 


The fork shall be held rigidly from the extreme end of 
the handle/shank and supported in the middle of the 
overall length in such a way that it is approximately 
horizontal. A load of 1 kg in case of pastry fork and 
load of 1.5 kg in case of table/serving, fish and dessert 
forks shall then be applied at the extreme end of the 
prongs for 2 min and then removed. The permanent 
deflection shall be measured after removal of the load. 
It shall not exceed 8 mm. 


7.3 Test for Forks with Hollow Handle 


Hollow handles after fitting shall be immersed for 30 s 
in clean air-free water maintained at 80°C. They shall 
not show any expulsion of air bubbles. 


7.4 Tests for Forks with Plastic Handles 
7.4.1 Boiling 


The fork shall be immersed for one hour in a boiling 
5 percent soap solution, then rinsed immediately in 


IS 16218 : 2014 


water at 15°C to 20°C and then dried for an hour in an 
oven maintained at 60°C. This procedure shall be 
repeated four times. On completion of test, the handle 
shall not show any sign of cracking, chipping or 
discoloring of the plastics and the tang shall neither 
become loose nor there be any damage. 


7.4.2 Impact 


This test shall be conducted after the boiling test. The 
fork shall be held with the handle facing downwards 
and dropped from a height of 1.2 m on to a concrete 
floor or a flat stone five times in succession. The handle 
shall not show any sign of cracking, breaking or 
chipping of the plastics and tang shall neither become 
loose nor shall there be any damage. 


7.4.3 Staining 


7.4.3.1 The plastics handle shall be cut into three 
pieces and each piece shall be immersed in one of the 
following solutions maintained at room temperature: 


a) Sodium chloride solution, 10 percent (w/v); 
b) Acetic acid solution, 5 percent (v/v); and 
c) Sodium carbonate solution, 2 percent (w/v). 


7.4.3.2 Each piece shall be taken out after 24 h, rinsed 
with tap water and wiped with a dry cloth. It shall then 
be examined and immersed again in the same solution. 
This process shall be repeated seven times. During and 
at the end of seven days test there shall be no 
perceptible change in the appearance of the plastic 
material. 


8 SAMPLING 


The number of forks to be selected from a lot for 
ascertaining conformity to this standard shall be as 
agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 
A suitable sampling scheme and criteria for conformity 
for forks is given in Table 1. 


8.1 Lot 


In any consignment, all the forks of the same type of 
handle, shape and size, manufactured from the same 
material under relatively similar conditions of 
manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a 
lot. 


8.2 For ascertaining the conformity to the 
requirements of this standard the test shall be conducted 
separately for each lot. 


8.3 The number of forks to be selected from a lot for 
ascertaining conformity to the requirements of this 
standard shall be according to Table 1. The forks in the 
sample shall be selected at random from the lot. If the 
forks are packed in cartons, as a first step at least 25 percent 
of the cartons, shall be selected at random and then from 


IS 16218 : 2014 


Table 1 Sampling Size and Criteria for Conformity 
(Clauses 8, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5) 


SI No. No. of Forks in a Lot For Clause No. 4 and 6.1 For Clause No. 6.2 and 7 
Sample Size Acceptance Number Sub-Sample Size Acceptance Number

each selected carton, equal number of forks be taken out 
at random so as to make the required sample size. 


8.4 The fork selected at random according to 8.3 shall 
be examined for the requirements of 4 and 6.1. A fork 
failing to satisfy any one or more of these requirements 
shall be regarded as defective. The lot shall be 
considered as conformity to the requirements of 4 
and 6.1, if the number of defectives forks in the sample 
does not exceed the number given in col 3 of Table 1. 


8.5 If the lot conforms to the requirements of 8.4, a 
sub-sample of size given in col 4 of Table 1 shall be 
taken from the forks selected as in 8.3. Each of fork in 
the sub-sample shall be tested for the requirements 
given in 6.2 and 7. A fork not satisfying any one or 
more of the requirements given in 6.2 and 7 shall be 
regarded as defective. The sample shall be considered 
to conform to the requirements given in 6.2 and 7 if 
number of defectives in sub-sample does not exceed 
the numbers given in col 5 of Table 1. 


9 MARKING 


9.1 Each fork shall be legibly marked with the 
following on underside of the handle preferably by 
engraving or etching: 

a) Type of fork; 

b) Material of fork; 

c) Material grade; 


d) Type of handle; 


e) Manufacturer’s name, initials or registered 
trade-mark; 


f) Made in India; and 


g) Batch No./Date of manufacturing if desired 
by the purchaser. 


Example: Table / SS / 304 / Plastic / XX Pvt 
Ltd / Made in India / YYY 


9.2 BIS Certification Marking 


9.2.1 Each fork may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


9.2.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provision of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the license for 
the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers, may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


10 PACKING 


The forks shall be wrapped in soft tissue paper or wax 
paper or suitable polythene bags and packed in cartons. 
The number of forks to be packed in one carton shall 
be at the discretion of the manufacturers. The cartons 
shall bear the type and number of forks packed, the 
name of the manufacturer, batch number and the 
country of the manufacturer. 


IS 16218 : 2014

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MED 33 (1107).
